hypothesis: Current S coordinates drive associative lookup, all-corner missing reduction and same-cycle advance. Advance feeds both RAM chip enables and req_ready/input frame invalidation. Register complete lookup results before issue; use only registered L hit/miss/addresses for RAM issue and upstream capacity.

changes.stages: S descriptor -> L registered lookup -> M synchronous RAM return -> R held output
changes.hit_throughput: S/L/M/R accept concurrent moves; warmed512 consecutive input accepts verified with no req_ready bubbles. Warm64 costs72 total UI cycles versus previous71.
l_payload: missing flag plus victim/found/missing key snapshot
changes.miss_ownership: L retains its descriptor throughout fills. After every final tile write, l_relookup fences further reads/fills while recapturing all ways, missing state and protected replacement selection against updated tags.
changes.frame_key: Only S processing with L space may change frame_key and invalidate all tags. A future S frame cannot invalidate a pending old-frame L miss. A prior L hit issues its last RAM read on the same edge as new-frame invalidation; subsequent fill waits until M drains.
changes.boundary: Read-right phase uses registered L boundary flag derived from unequal x word indices, equivalent to the original left/right RAM-address boundary for legal clipped/nearest coordinates.
changes.memory: Original two synchronous RAM read ports and one shared A-port fill write retained; RAM and read data have no reset. Read/write mutual exclusion asserted in tests.

timing_isolation_red_green: Between clock edges, changing lookup-valid tags must not change input capacity or RAM read enable. Original RTL fails this requirement; new registered lookup passes. Actual timing closure remains pending physical implementation.

latency_budget.miss_extra_cycles: One L capture before first miss fill; one registered relookup edge after each installed tile. No additional DDR commands for a given descriptor trace.
latency_budget.integration_risk: Native full-frame budget is tight (~16.545ms). Added miss-only cycles can affect publication interval and must be measured by root full60; this local result does not claim60fps.
